newsitem.title: USA: Ametek Inc says expects record year.
newsitem.headline: Ametek Inc says expects record year.

text.p: Ametek Inc said on Tuesday that it was recovering from short term weaknesses in certain markets, but that it expected 1997 to be another record year.

"The market conditions a year ago were considerably stronger; today, we are recovering from near-term weakness in certain key markets, said Walter Blankley, chairman and chief executive officer of the company.

"A decline in our specialty metals business was the primary factor accounting for lower first quarter sales and operating income for the Industrial Materials Group, compared with the year-ago period," he added.
Blankley also said that the company's first quarter results were in line with previously stated expectations.

"We expect a strong second half of this year to compensate for a modestly improved first-half performance," he said. "We continue to be confident that our 1997 performance will mark a fourth consecutive year of record sales and earnings."
In 1996, Ametek had record sales of $869 million and achieved a third consecutive year of record income and earnings per share from continuing operations.
Ameteck manufactures electrical and electromechanical products and materials engineered for niche markets, with operations in the United States, Europe, Asia, and Mexico.
